name: Joe Moss
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Extend (San Francisco)
profile: Joe Moss co-founded Extend, a San Francisco company that sells product-protection plans (extended warranties) and shipping protection through online merchants. CEO Woody Levin leads the company. Extend began selling in 2019 and raised a $260M Series C at a valuation of over $1.6B in May 2021. Moss leads product.
interesting_fact: Extend became a unicorn in about 27 months of operation. CEO Woody Levin pitched it as the 'Apple Care' for everything that isn't an Apple product.
notes: Low public profile. Moss's prior roles (reportedly DocuSign product and an earlier startup) appear only on aggregator sites and could not be verified, so they are left out. No published press email was found on extend.com. The best route is the company contact form, or via CEO Woody Levin.

name: Rick Song
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Persona (identity verification platform, San Francisco)
profile: Rick Song spent about five years at Square as an engineer and early Square Capital team member. In 2018 he co-founded Persona with CTO Charles Yeh to build configurable identity-verification building blocks. In April 2025 Persona raised a $200M Series D led by Founders Fund and Ribbit at a $2B valuation, pitching a 'verified identity layer' for an AI-agent internet.
interesting_fact: Persona's $200M Series D (April 2025) valued it at $2B, up from $1.5B in its 2021 Series C. The pitch is building the verified identity layer for an increasingly AI-driven internet.
deep_cut_fact: At Square he worked on lending fraud at Square Capital and on trust and safety for the Caviar food-delivery business, which exposed him to many identity-verification use cases. He calls himself 'slightly obsessed' with pre-mortems and jokes that Persona is 'an entire company of people who have never done startups'.
notes: The press email came from the withpersona.com/about page text as returned by search; a direct fetch of the page was blocked (403). He has done podcasts (First Round 'In Depth' ep. 22, Product Market Fit Show), so he is receptive to founder-story interviews.

name: Oliver Kent-Braham
current_role: Co-founder and CEO (also described as co-CEO), Marshmallow (UK car and home insurer for newcomers)
profile: Oliver Kent-Braham is a south-west Londoner and briefly a banker at Investec. In 2017 he co-founded Marshmallow with his twin Alexander and engineer David Goate to make car insurance fairer for people who have moved to the UK. Marshmallow became a licensed insurer in 2021. Its April 2025 $90M raise valued it at about $2B, with roughly 1M customers and a ~$500M revenue run rate.
interesting_fact: Marshmallow insures roughly one million people, up from about 100,000 in 2021, and says it is profitable on a ~$500M annual revenue run rate. Kent-Braham calls migration 'a huge opportunity'.
deep_cut_fact: In the early days the founders worked from the lobby of a Virgin Active gym. Kent-Braham paid for an £80 membership, which got the team a desk plus sauna and steam room access: 'the cheapest office space'. The idea came from a Canadian friend who kept getting sky-high car insurance quotes.
notes: His twin Alexander is the other co-founder (internal/product side); Oliver handles external matters and fundraising. No press email was found on marshmallow.com. Sources vary on the founding year (2016 or 2017).

name: Peter Godman
current_role: Unknown; former co-founder, founding CEO and later CTO of Qumulo (left November 2018)
profile: Peter Godman is a Seattle systems engineer. At Isilon he led several major releases of the OneFS distributed file system, then was VP engineering and CEO at Corensic. In 2012 he co-founded Qumulo, a scale-out file-storage company, with fellow Isilon alumni Neil Fachan and Aaron Passey. He served as CEO until Bill Richter took over in 2016, then as CTO until he left in late 2018.
interesting_fact: He is credited with inventing 18 patented technologies. At Corensic he brought what was billed as the world's first thin-hypervisor-based product to market.
deep_cut_fact: When he left Qumulo after nearly seven years, CEO Bill Richter called him 'a visionary, an inspiration and a good friend' and wished him 'a well deserved break, time with his family and his next adventure.'
notes: No public reporting on his activities since leaving Qumulo in 2018 was found, so alive is marked unknown (no death reports found either). Very low public profile; no verified personal site or social accounts found. Relevant to the data-center angle as a storage and file-system veteran.

name: Adam Crawshaw
current_role: Unverified; co-founder and former President of Assembly (e-commerce software group behind Helium 10, Refersion and Pacvue)
profile: Adam Crawshaw is listed as a co-founder of Assembly, an e-commerce software roll-up formed around 2018. Assembly bought Refersion and Amazon-seller tool Helium 10 in 2020, then the ad platform Pacvue in 2021, and later unified its products under the Pacvue brand. In July 2020 he was quoted as President of Assembly. His current role could not be verified from official sources.
interesting_fact: Assembly assembled Helium 10, the Amazon-seller toolkit, and Pacvue, the commerce-advertising platform, into one software group serving brands that sell on online marketplaces.
notes: Identity marked uncertain: the only official mention found is a 2020 Assembly press release naming him 'President of Assembly'. Co-founder status and later roles (Refersion GM, Helium 10 GM) come only from aggregator profiles. Don't confuse this Assembly with the ad agency Assembly Global. No published contact found.

name: Kağan Sümer
current_role: Former founder and CEO of Gorillas (Berlin). Reported since 2023 to be building a new health-tech startup, Mirror, with Gorillas co-founder Uğur Samut (current status unverified).
profile: Istanbul-born Kağan Sümer worked at Rocket Internet's B2B food group in Berlin, then in May 2020 founded Gorillas, a 10-minute grocery delivery service using bike couriers. It became a unicorn in about nine months, reportedly Germany's fastest. Rival Getir bought Gorillas in December 2022 for about $1.2B, and Sümer left. German press reported in 2023 that he was starting a health-tech company.
interesting_fact: Gorillas went from founding in May 2020 to a $1B+ valuation in about nine months, which Wikipedia describes as the fastest any German company had done so.
deep_cut_fact: Rocket Internet ignored six of his job applications in one month before later hiring him. He once cycled from Istanbul to China, captained Turkey's youth water polo team, and spent 88 of his 100 euros on a bike when he arrived in Berlin. Gorillas began as 'Get Goodies' in his living room.
notes: Gorillas no longer exists (Getir wound it down in 2024), so there is no company press channel. Mirror was reported by deutsche-startups.de (May 2023): https://www.deutsche-startups.de/2023/05/02/gorillas-gruender-klonen-aware/. Aggregator listings of newer ventures (Sugar, Nutz) are unverified. A strong fit for the entrepreneurship angle (bikes, logistics, blitzscaling).

name: Takeshi Otsuka
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Producer & SVP, Playco (instant-play gaming, HQ Tokyo)
profile: Takeshi Otsuka is a Japanese game producer who led DeNA's Mobage mobile social gaming platform (2005-2015), which Playco says generated over $1B in revenue. He moved to the US in 2011 for roles at DeNA West and N3TWORK. In 2020 he co-founded Playco with Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron, WebSocket co-inventor Michael Carter and Teddy Cross. Playco builds games playable instantly inside social and messaging apps and was valued at $1B in its Series A.
interesting_fact: Playco's co-founders include Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron and Michael Carter, co-inventor of HTML5 WebSockets. The company is headquartered in Tokyo but distributed-first, with founders split across Seoul, Tokyo, San Francisco and LA.
deep_cut_fact: He produced 'Kaito Royale' (2009), a mobile social game whose success helped spark Japan's mobile social gaming boom (over a thousand such games were released in 2010) and which also became a TV show. N3TWORK CEO Neil Young called him a '10x-er'.
notes: Second source for the Kaito Royale TV show and the '10x-er' quote: https://www.pocketgamer.biz/n3twork-hires-takeshi-otsuka/. No published press email was found on play.co. Low English-language media profile.

name: Ze Yongjun
current_role: Co-founder, Xiaoe-tech (小鹅通, Shenzhen knowledge-commerce / private-domain SaaS); current title not found
profile: Xiaoe-tech's 2026 Hong Kong IPO filing coverage names co-founders Wang Lianghu and Zeng Yongjun (曾勇军), both former Tencent T3 senior R&D engineers, alongside founder-chairman-CEO Bao Chunjian (ex-Tencent data-centre director). Founded in 2015, Xiaoe-tech sells SaaS tools for online courses and private-domain e-commerce. Tencent invested in its 2020 Series C. It reported 2025 revenue of about RMB 608M and is pursuing an HKEX listing.
interesting_fact: Xiaoe-tech's founding team is heavily ex-Tencent. Founder Bao Chunjian ran Tencent's data centre business, two co-founders were Tencent T3 senior engineers, and another co-founder (Yu Ganli) worked on QQ Zone product development.
notes: 'Ze Yongjun' appears to be a romanization of 曾勇军 (Zeng Yongjun), a co-founder named in 36Kr's May 2026 IPO coverage. The match is likely but not confirmed. He is not among the listed executive directors (Bao Chunjian, Wang Tiebo, Hu Yabei, Zhou Shikun). Very low public profile; the best route is via the company once IR contacts appear in the HKEX prospectus.

name: Spike Lipkin
current_role: Co-founder and CEO of Newfront, now part of WTW after WTW completed the acquisition in January 2026. At WTW he focuses on integration, client development, talent acquisition and technology.
profile: Spike Lipkin was a Blackstone investor on the startup team behind Invitation Homes, then one of Opendoor's first employees. In 2017 he co-founded Newfront, a San Francisco insurance brokerage built on its own technology covering business insurance and employee benefits. WTW agreed to buy Newfront in December 2025 and completed the roughly $1.3bn acquisition in January 2026; Lipkin joined WTW.
interesting_fact: WTW's acquisition of Newfront was reported at about $1.3bn including contingent consideration. Lipkin built the tech-enabled broker from a 2017 start into one of the largest venture-backed deals in insurance brokerage.
deep_cut_fact: Before insurance he was on Blackstone's startup team that built Invitation Homes into the largest US owner of single-family rental homes. He then joined Opendoor when it had five people. Both jobs exposed him firsthand to how painful buying insurance was.
notes: Now inside WTW, a public company, so media requests likely route through WTW media relations (contact not verified this session). He has appeared on podcasts (Category Visionaries, June 2023). Insurance Business named him a 2019 Young Gun at age 31.

name: Raymond Chu
current_role: Co-founder, Aleo (zero-knowledge privacy blockchain); described as an engineer on Aleo's core node software (snarkVM/snarkOS). Exact current title not verified.
profile: Raymond Chu co-founded Aleo Systems in December 2019 with Howard Wu, Michael Beller and Collin Chin. Aleo builds a layer-1 blockchain for private applications using zero-knowledge proofs, rooted in the Berkeley Zexe research, and is backed by investors including a16z. Mainnet launched in September 2024. Chu is an engineering co-founder rather than a public face.
interesting_fact: Aleo was created as 'the first platform for fully private applications', and its name stands for Autonomous Ledger Executions Off-chain. The design grew out of the Zexe zero-knowledge research at UC Berkeley.
deep_cut_fact: He is a hands-on engineer: GitHub shows Raymond Chu (handle raychu86) committing code to Aleo's trusted-setup ceremony software (AleoNet/aleo-setup) in November 2020, ahead of the network's launch.
notes: Very low media profile; Howard Wu (now CEO of Provable) is Aleo's public spokesperson. His commit email appears in git metadata, but it was not published as a contact and is deliberately excluded.

name: Eitan Yanovsky
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Optibus (AI-based public-transit planning and scheduling software, Tel Aviv)
profile: Eitan Yanovsky studied math and computer science at Ben-Gurion University, where he met Amos Haggiag. He was later an R&D team leader at GigaSpaces. In 2014 the pair founded Optibus to solve bus and transit scheduling with optimization algorithms. Optibus software is used in over 1,000 cities, and the company had raised about $170M by 2022. Yanovsky leads research and technology.
interesting_fact: The idea came from co-founder Amos Haggiag's father, a long-time CFO of Israeli bus company Kavim, who challenged him to write software to plan bus routes. The founders treated it as a traveling-salesman-style puzzle.
deep_cut_fact: Optibus was a side project for nearly a decade: Yanovsky (at GigaSpaces) and Haggiag (at Microsoft Israel) kept 'toying with this idea during our free time', testing it on data from small Israeli bus companies, before quitting to found the company.
notes: Optibus's about page confirms him as Co-Founder and CTO. Relevant to the energy angle: Optibus also does electric-bus fleet planning (not checked in detail). CEO Amos Haggiag is the more public co-founder.

name: Rahul Dash
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Purplle (Indian online beauty retailer and brand house, Mumbai); role as reported in 2023
profile: Rahul Dash is an IIT Kharagpur graduate who then went to IIM Ahmedabad and worked at Tata, where the Purplle idea took shape. He co-founded Purplle with Manish Taneja (CEO) and Suyash Katyayani (CTO). The trio pooled about Rs 40 lakh of savings to start it. Purplle sells beauty products online and through its own brands, and became a unicorn valued at about $1B.
interesting_fact: Purplle's three co-founders started the company by pooling just Rs 40 lakh (about $50k) of their own savings. It later became a ~$1B (about Rs 8,200 crore) beauty unicorn competing with Nykaa.
notes: Sources conflict on his pre-Purplle employer: DNA says Tata (aggregators say Tata Power strategy and business development), while indiacsr.in says McKinsey. Left out of the deep-cut for that reason. If Tata Power is confirmed, it is a natural energy-podcast hook. CEO Manish Taneja is the public face. Current role not re-verified after 2023.

name: Howard Yeh
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Revenue Officer, HealthCare.com (New York). His roles there went Co-Founder, then CEO, then COO, then CRO.
profile: Howard Yeh is a Penn graduate who started as a Merrill Lynch media investment banker and was a VC at VantagePoint. He co-founded BrokersWeb, an insurance ad network that made the Inc. 500 twice and was acquired by Vantage Media in 2011. He then co-founded HealthCare.com, a health-insurance marketplace that has raised $200M+ across Series A to C, and he still blogs on ACA, Medicare Advantage and insurtech.
interesting_fact: BrokersWeb, his first insurance company, grew revenue from $16M in 2010 to $55M in 2011 before Vantage Media acquired it. It was twice on the Inc. 500.
deep_cut_fact: Between BrokersWeb and HealthCare.com he co-founded ContactUs.com (2012-2015), a SaaS tool for better website contact forms and lead capture. He describes its sale to WorkWave in 2015 as a 'bite-sized acquisition'. He also writes on his blog about Asian American leadership and entrepreneurship.
notes: Very accessible: he runs an active personal blog (posts through March 2026) on healthcare markets, AI and founder stories, which is a natural hook for outreach. NYC-based. Don Loonam became HealthCare.com CEO in March 2021.

name: Gaurab Chakrabarti
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Solugen (Houston chemicals-from-biology company)
profile: Gaurab Chakrabarti is a physician-scientist (Forbes 30 Under 30; author on 20+ publications and patents). In 2016 he co-founded Solugen with MIT chemical engineer Sean Hunt. Solugen's 'Bioforge' plants combine enzymes and metal catalysts to turn corn sugar into chemicals such as hydrogen peroxide and organic acids that normally come from petroleum. It is building a second Bioforge in Marshall, Minnesota.
interesting_fact: In June 2024 Solugen got a conditional commitment for a $213.6M DOE Loan Programs Office loan guarantee for Bioforge Marshall. It is a ~500,000 sq ft plant next to an ADM corn facility, which DOE called its largest single bioindustrial manufacturing investment since the 2022 biotech executive order.
deep_cut_fact: Solugen started on a $10,000 MIT grant meant to cover salaries, rent and equipment, in a $150/month space near the Houston airport. Chakrabarti jokingly called himself 'the Heisenberg of hydrogen peroxide'. Seed investor Seth Bannon of Fifty Years called it one of the 'sketchiest' labs he had seen.
notes: Strong fit for the energy and decarbonization angle. Per a Climate Now / MCJ account, he and Hunt reportedly met at a poker game in Texas (not checked against a primary source). Whether the DOE loan guarantee closed was not verified.
